solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Ending piece about Republican revolution (5)

indicatorNotes.about: 'About' means around, so OBIT stands all round the R

blocks.note: an obit (obituary) is a newspaper piece about someone's end

annotation.surface: A commentator's closing article on a Republican uprising.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ending piece" reads like a final chapter or a chess endgame; it is an obituary, a piece written about a life's ending.
annotation.definitionFit: An orbit is one full revolution around a body.

entries.clue: Become inflexible whenever restricted by leaderless authoritarian (6)

indicatorNotes.restricted by: Something restricted is confined, so IF is held within the walls of OSSY

blocks.note: BOSSY without its first letter B
'if' can mean 'whenever', as in 'if it rains, I stay in'

annotation.surface: Someone stiffens up whenever a bossy person reins them in.
annotation.walkthrough: "Whenever" looks like a time word in the surface; its job is the tiny conditional that goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: To ossify is literally to turn to bone, and figuratively to become rigid and set in one's ways.

entries.clue: Reward cake with characteristic features (7,6)

blocks.note: a brownie is a chocolate cake
a person's good points are their features

annotation.surface: A cake handed out as a prize for having the right qualities.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a baking contest; the two halves simply sit side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Brownie points are the notional credit you earn for pleasing someone, a reward of sorts.

entries.clue: Fish caught in grate, tragically (5)

indicatorNotes.caught in: the answer is held inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A fish gets stuck in a drain grate, a sad end.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma is surface decoration; the letters run straight across it.
annotation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small tropical fish popular in aquariums.

entries.clue: Victoria’s help with delivery from new coal depots (6,4)

indicatorNotes.new: the letters are made into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Queen Victoria gets her coal delivered from fresh depots.
annotation.walkthrough: Victoria is not the queen but Victoria in Canada or Australia, places that say postal code where Britain says postcode.
annotation.definitionFit: A postal code is what helps the mail get delivered in Victoria.

entries.clue: Bone from last bit of meat found in rice dish (7)

indicatorNotes.last bit of: take the final letter of meat
indicatorNotes.found in: the T goes inside the rice dish

blocks.note: paella is the Spanish rice dish

annotation.surface: A bone turns up in the meat of a paella.
annotation.walkthrough: "Found in" reads as a bone turning up in your dinner, which is exactly the instruction: the letter goes inside the dish.
annotation.definitionFit: The kneecap is one specific bone, so the general word covers it as a definition by category.

entries.clue: Put on another thing believed to cover mess up (12)

indicatorNotes.to cover: To cover something is to spread over it on every side, so SUPPOSED wraps round ERIM
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' turns MIRE backwards

annotation.surface: Someone puts on a fresh layer they think will hide the mess.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mess up" reads as a phrasal verb, to spoil, but splits into a noun and its instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Superimposed means placed on top of something else.

entries.clue: A book with blotches remains dry (8)

annotation.surface: A blotchy old book whose pages have stayed dry.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dry" suggests paper kept out of the damp; it means off the drink.
annotation.definitionFit: To abstain is to stay dry, drinking no alcohol.

entries.clue: To begin with, can everybody list everything by name? (5)

indicatorNotes.To begin with: take the opening letter of each word

annotation.surface: A question about whether everyone can list everything alphabetically by name.
annotation.walkthrough: "By name" looks like part of the listing instruction; "by" gives the B and "name" is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A 'name' in the sense of a famous person, as in 'big names at the party', which is what the informal CELEB means.

entries.clue: Record bonus periodically leading to anger and dismay (10)

indicatorNotes.periodically: Something that happens periodically recurs at regular intervals, so the letters are taken at every second step

annotation.surface: A bonus on your record that brings anger and dismay.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dismay" is a verb here, like discourage.
annotation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to dismay them, sapping their confidence.

entries.clue: People not taking away snakes (6)

blocks.note: people who add rather than subtract
the adder is Britain's venomous snake

annotation.surface: People who leave the snakes where they are.
annotation.walkthrough: "Taking away" reads as removing something; in arithmetic it is subtraction, and its opposite is adding.
annotation.definitionFit: Adders both add up numbers and are snakes.

entries.clue: Kick around entrance to station after outdoor event (7)

indicatorNotes.after: 'After' means following in order, so the S is written behind DISCUS

blocks.note: the discus is a field event in athletics

annotation.surface: Kicking a ball around a station entrance after an outdoor event.
annotation.walkthrough: "Kick around" looks physical; it means to talk an idea over.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: kicking a proposal around means batting it back and forth in talk.

entries.clue: Hired gun deployed to protect British city (9)

indicatorNotes.deployed: the letters are sent out into a new order
indicatorNotes.to protect: the anagram wraps round the B

annotation.surface: A mercenary sent in to guard a British city.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram EDINURGH takes the B inside, between N and U.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Scottish capital is one instance of a city.

entries.clue: South of France, an Arab League nation (5)

annotation.surface: A Mediterranean-sounding description of an Arab League member.
annotation.walkthrough: "South of France" looks like the Riviera; it means the French word for south.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the African state south of Egypt joined the Arab League in 1956.

entries.clue: Kittens now gone astray somewhere in North London (5,9)

indicatorNotes.gone astray: the letters have wandered out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, doubling as part of the indicator

annotation.surface: A lost-kittens notice pinned up in a North London street.
annotation.walkthrough: "Gone" does two jobs: its letters are fodder, and with "astray" it tells you to scramble. Stoke Newington is a district of the London borough of Hackney.
annotation.definitionFit: A deliberately vague definition by location: the district lies in Hackney, in the north of inner London.

entries.clue: Two articles of clothing for baseball player (9)

annotation.surface: A baseball player is issued a two-piece kit.
annotation.walkthrough: One fragment supplies both pieces: find two garments that join into a single word, reading 'for' as a link.
annotation.definitionFit: An American sports term: the fielder stationed between second and third base is named after his position.

entries.clue: Smug Tories ultimately sad if lefties hammered (4-9)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of Tories
indicatorNotes.hammered: the letters are beaten out of shape

annotation.surface: Smug Conservatives would be sorry to see the Left beaten at the polls.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hammered" reads as defeated in an election; here it batters the letters into a new order.
annotation.definitionFit: Self-satisfied means smugly pleased with oneself.

entries.clue: Cool guy declared this is how to reach for the stars? (3,4)

annotation.definition: this is how to reach for the stars?

indicatorNotes.declared: said out loud, so go by the sound

blocks.note: to fan something is to cool it
a guy is a male, which sounds like mail

annotation.surface: A cool dude announces his route to fame.
annotation.walkthrough: The stars are celebrities, not the night sky: fan mail is how admirers reach them.
annotation.definitionFit: Fan mail is the letters fans send to reach famous people.

entries.clue: Back door badly broken by back of steel barrier (9)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are put together wrongly
indicatorNotes.broken by: the anagram is split by the L

annotation.surface: A back door has been smashed in, perhaps with a steel bar.
annotation.walkthrough: "Back" appears twice doing different jobs: once as fodder, once as the last-letter signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A roadblock is a barrier set across a road.

entries.clue: Duke abandoning port city (5)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: To abandon is to walk out and leave behind, so the D departs from DURBAN

blocks.note: Durban is the South African port

annotation.surface: A duke sails away from a port city.
annotation.walkthrough: "Port city" reads as one phrase; "port" is DURBAN and "city" alone is the definition, used as an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Urban means of a city, as in city life or urban life.

entries.clue: Executive chap beset by widespread rage, unfortunately (7,7)

indicatorNotes.beset by: MAN is surrounded by the other pieces
indicatorNotes.unfortunately: RAGE comes out in a bad order

annotation.surface: A boss surrounded by fury on all sides.
annotation.walkthrough: "Executive chap" reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at "Executive"; the chap is the one who gets surrounded.
annotation.definitionFit: A job title standing for its holder: the person who runs a whole business is one of its executives.

entries.clue: Enthusiastic former taxi company worker? (9)

annotation.surface: A cheerful ex-employee of a cab firm.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the surface's former Uber worker is a split-up word, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of enthusiasm and energy.

entries.clue: Smooth movement of legs said to need manipulation (8)

indicatorNotes.to need manipulation: the letters must be handled into a new order

annotation.surface: A physiotherapist's note on a gliding stride that needs treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: "Smooth movement of legs" reads as one phrase, but "legs" is fodder and the definition stops at "movement".
annotation.definitionFit: A glissade is a smooth gliding step in ballet.

entries.clue: Patent medicine is in no way odd (7)

annotation.surface: A claim that a quack remedy is perfectly normal.
annotation.walkthrough: "In no way" reads as a phrase meaning 'not at all'; "in" is surface only and the pieces are NO, way and odd.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin 'our own': quacks sold their secret remedies as patent medicines.

entries.clue: Method helping self-control (10)

blocks.note: a ration is a helping of food

annotation.surface: A technique that aids self-discipline.
annotation.walkthrough: "Helping" reads as a verb (aiding); it is a noun, a portion of food.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: keeping one's appetites within bounds is the restraint the definition names.

entries.clue: One administering software left in charge and set up schedule (10)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, ROTA is turned upwards

blocks.note: a rota is a duty schedule

annotation.surface: An IT administrator arranging a work rota.
annotation.walkthrough: "Administering" suggests running software; it means applying something, like a brush putting on ointment.
annotation.definitionFit: An applicator is a device that administers or applies a substance.

entries.clue: Driving force baffled poor, heartless Polonius (10)

indicatorNotes.heartless: POOR loses its middle letters OO
indicatorNotes.baffled: Someone baffled is thoroughly confused, and confused letters lose their order

blocks.note: POOR with its middle OO removed

annotation.surface: Hamlet's meddling old counsellor Polonius, baffled and heartless.
annotation.walkthrough: "Heartless" seems to describe Polonius, but it is attached to "poor" and empties it.
annotation.definitionFit: Propulsion is the force that drives something forward.

entries.clue: Magazine’s short metaphor, possibly about football? (9,5)

indicatorNotes.about: 'About' as in 'about turn', a soldier facing the other way, so TROP reverses

blocks.note: The Spectator is a British weekly magazine; with the 's
a metaphor is one kind of trope; cut short

annotation.surface: A magazine's pithy figure of speech about football.
annotation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a long-running British political weekly. "Possibly" goes with "metaphor": a metaphor is an example of a trope.
annotation.definitionFit: Football is a sport watched by crowds of spectators; the question mark marks the definition by example.

entries.clue: Experienced four seasons in one day, perhaps? (5-7)

annotation.definition: Experienced four seasons in one day, perhaps?

blocks.note: read as living through spring, summer, autumn and winter, and meant as getting through four series of a TV show
the stock phrase for wildly changeable weather, turned into a marathon on the sofa

annotation.surface: A day of wildly changing weather: sun, rain, wind and snow.
annotation.walkthrough: "Four seasons in one day" is a stock phrase for changeable weather; the seasons are series of a TV show.
annotation.definitionFit: To binge-watch is to view many episodes of a series in one sitting.

entries.clue: Bags very nearly start to putrefy sitting in dump for so long (6-3)

indicatorNotes.sitting in: Something sitting in a place is inside it, so OODLE and P rest within TIP

blocks.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
bags (of) = oodles, a lot; minus its last letter S

annotation.surface: Rubbish bags left rotting at the tip for ages.
annotation.walkthrough: "So long" reads as a length of time; it is a farewell, and toodle-pip is old-fashioned British for goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip, like so long, is a way of saying goodbye.

entries.clue: Outlet plugged into one new gold Tesla? (8)

indicatorNotes.plugged into: VENT is inserted into the other letters

annotation.surface: Plugging a shiny new gold Tesla car into a power outlet.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tesla is not the electric car but Nikola Tesla, the inventor it is named after; the question mark signals the example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: Nikola Tesla devised the AC induction motor.

entries.clue: Drop, having no power to thrust forward (5)

indicatorNotes.having no: A word having no power has lost its P, so the P is struck out

annotation.surface: A car loses power and drops, then lurches ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: The first letter goes: PLUNGE becomes LUNGE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a fencer's sudden forward thrust with the sword.

entries.clue: Equality is true thing that sticks out (8)

blocks.note: true = level or even, as a carpenter says
a ness is a headland jutting into the sea

annotation.surface: A slogan asserting that equality really stands out.
annotation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland (Loch Ness is a lake, but ness itself means a promontory).
annotation.definitionFit: Evenness means equality, with no side ahead.

entries.clue: Increasingly arrogant eccentrics losing face over row (8)

indicatorNotes.over: Turned over as a page is flipped, so OONS reads right to left

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

annotation.surface: Stuck-up oddballs lose face over a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: "Row" reads as a quarrel; it is a line of seats, a tier.
annotation.definitionFit: Snootier means more snooty, more arrogant.

entries.clue: Fashionable male with striking social media activity? (13)

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer

annotation.surface: A trendy man posting eye-catching content online.
annotation.walkthrough: "Striking" looks like an adjective for the male; it is a verb, and the male is an animal, STAG.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: posting photos to the Instagram app is one kind of social media use.

entries.clue: Computer user cracked the highest level of authority? (7,5)

annotation.surface: A hacker breaks into the top-level admin account.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cracked" and "highest level of authority" suggest a hacked system with admin rights; it is the top court of law.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the top tribunal is the final legal authority, and the question mark admits there are other kinds of authority.

entries.clue: Nonchalant attempt to disregard the second person suffering (8)

indicatorNotes.to disregard the second: the second letter of TRY is left out

blocks.note: TRY without its second letter R

annotation.surface: A half-hearted effort to ignore a second person in pain.
annotation.walkthrough: "The second person" looks like 'you' in grammar; "the second" belongs to the deletion and "person suffering" is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain sense: someone hurt in an accident or war, the victim who suffers.

entries.clue: Make new modifications to study with lack of partiality (8)

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it

annotation.surface: Revising a study to remove bias.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lack of partiality" is a noun phrase standing for the adjective JUST; the clue leans on the sense rather than the grammar.
annotation.definitionFit: The prefix RE- supplies 'new' and ADJUST supplies 'make modifications to'.

entries.clue: “Top 10 Musicians” possibly featuring unknown composer (5)

indicatorNotes.featuring: A show featuring a guest has them in it, so LIST includes the Z

annotation.surface: A chart countdown that includes a mystery composer.
annotation.walkthrough: Z goes between S and T. The quotation marks make "Top 10 Musicians" look like a title; it is just an example of a list.
annotation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and pianist.

entries.clue: Ostentatiously modern bubbly few in England drunk (10)

indicatorNotes.bubbly: FEW fizzes into a new order
indicatorNotes.in: EWF goes inside the other anagram
indicatorNotes.drunk: ENGLAND staggers into a new order

annotation.surface: A trendy fizz that only a few in England drink.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bubbly" looks like champagne, the drink the surface is about, but it is an instruction to scramble the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Newfangled means showily new, often said disapprovingly.

entries.clue: The way in which you’d ideally see some cricket? (6-6)

annotation.definition: The way in which you’d ideally see

blocks.clueFragment: The way in which you’d ideally see

blocks.note: Twenty20 is the short form of cricket, 20 overs a side

annotation.surface: How you would like to watch a cricket match.
annotation.walkthrough: Twenty20 (T20) is a short, fast format of cricket played over one evening.
annotation.definitionFit: Twenty-twenty vision is normal sharp sight, and Twenty20 is a cricket format.

entries.clue: Attendants from part of hospital in the same cohort as us? (9)

blocks.note: ENT = ear, nose and throat department

blocks.clueFragment: in the same cohort as us

annotation.surface: Hospital staff who are our contemporaries.
annotation.walkthrough: "Attendants" looks like hospital orderlies; it means a star's retinue.
annotation.definitionFit: An entourage is a group of attendants around an important person.

entries.clue: Key instrument briefly identified by GP? (5,5)

annotation.definition: Key instrument briefly identified by GP?

blocks.note: read as a vital medical tool, and meant as an instrument played with keys
read as a quick diagnosis by a family doctor, and meant as the two-letter short form used in music catalogues

annotation.surface: A doctor identifies a vital instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: GP looks like a family doctor (general practitioner) and "instrument" like a medical tool; GP is also the short form of grand piano, a keyboard instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: The large concert keyboard with a horizontal frame is written GP for short, which is the clue's whole joke.

entries.clue: Sanctimonious sort is pompous at heart and mostly tough? That makes sense! (8)

annotation.surface: A self-righteous type is pompous and hard-nosed, and someone finally gets it.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation "That makes sense!" reads as a comment on the clue itself; it is a piece of wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A Pharisee is a self-righteous, hypocritical person.

entries.clue: Muscle aiding flexibility that goes in both directions? (7)

indicatorNotes.goes in both directions?: A word that goes both ways reads identically left to right and right to left, which is the only wordplay here

blocks.note: The definition end: a muscle that turns a joint, such as those of the shoulder cuff.
The wordplay end: seven letters that read the same from either end.

annotation.surface: A muscle that lets a limb turn either way.
annotation.walkthrough: "Goes in both directions" seems to describe the muscle's motion; it describes the word, which reads the same both ways.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotator is a muscle that rotates a limb, as in the rotator cuff.

entries.clue: Was inclined to accept resistance, and became popular online (7)

indicatorNotes.to accept: To accept something is to take it in, so TENDED takes the R inside

annotation.surface: Someone reluctantly accepted pushback and then went viral.
annotation.walkthrough: The R goes in after the T.
annotation.definitionFit: A topic that trended was widely popular on social media.

entries.clue: Itch regularly occurring in front section, usually (3,3,4,4)

indicatorNotes.regularly: Regularly means at even intervals, so the letters are picked at every second step
indicatorNotes.occurring in: Something occurring in a place turns up inside it, so TH appears within FOREMOST PART

blocks.note: the foremost part is the front section

annotation.surface: An itch that keeps coming back at the front, as it tends to.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer's word breaks (3,3,4,4) hide the split: the inserted letters fall between FOR and EMOST, so FOREMOST disappears in the final phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: what holds in most cases holds usually, so the adverbial phrase and the adverb swap freely.

entries.clue: Tolerate extremely busy, low-cost air travel option (7)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the two end letters of busy

blocks.note: to stand something is to tolerate it

annotation.surface: Putting up with a crowded budget flight.
annotation.walkthrough: "Extremely busy" reads as very crowded; it means the extremes of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Flying standby means waiting for a spare seat, often at a lower fare.

entries.clue: Figure it seems initially futile to head north (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of it seems
indicatorNotes.to head north: in a down clue, NO GO reads upwards

blocks.note: the first letters of It Seems

annotation.surface: Heading north seems pointless from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: An isogon is a geometric figure with all angles equal; "Figure" is not a number or a person's shape.
annotation.definitionFit: An isogon is a polygon with equal angles, a figure in geometry.

entries.clue: Quiet, ill-mannered fuddy-duddy (5)

annotation.surface: A description of a stuffy, impolite old bore.
annotation.walkthrough: The irony is that a prude objects to rudeness.
annotation.definitionFit: A prude is a prim, easily shocked person, a fuddy-duddy.

entries.clue: One creating a nuisance over something saucy? (5)

blocks.note: a pest makes a nuisance of itself

annotation.surface: A pest making a fuss about something cheeky.
annotation.walkthrough: "Saucy" suggests cheek or innuendo; pesto is literally a sauce, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil sauce.

entries.clue: Get the jitters about eg your eulogy (9)

indicatorNotes.about: 'About' means around, so PANIC stands on both sides of EG and YR

blocks.note: to panic is to get the jitters

annotation.surface: Nerves before delivering a eulogy at a funeral.
annotation.walkthrough: "Your" is shortened the way letter-writers do (yr), and "eg" is used exactly as printed.
annotation.definitionFit: A panegyric is a speech of high praise, like a eulogy.

entries.clue: Third best grade from school graduate (5)

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales
MA = Master of Arts, a graduate

annotation.surface: A school leaver's mediocre mark.
annotation.walkthrough: "School" seems to belong with grades and graduates; it is a group of whales, a gam.
annotation.definitionFit: Gamma, the third Greek letter, is a third-class grade after alpha and beta.

entries.clue: A race contest with penultimate round withdrawn now and then (2,5)

blocks.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
the semi (semi-final) is the penultimate round

annotation.surface: A race whose semi-final has been cancelled.
annotation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
annotation.definitionFit: Two interchangeable idioms for something that happens occasionally, not all the time.

entries.clue: At first, teams of rescuers scour one core area (5)

indicatorNotes.At first: take the opening letter of each word

annotation.surface: Rescue teams search an area first.
annotation.walkthrough: "Core area" reads as a search zone; it is the core of the body.
annotation.definitionFit: The torso is the central part of the body, its core.

entries.clue: Lights requiring large amounts of current on street and a road (8,5)

annotation.surface: Street lighting that uses lots of electricity.
annotation.walkthrough: "On" places L AMPS after ST AND A RD, in an across clue. A standard lamp is British for a tall floor lamp.
annotation.definitionFit: Standard lamps are tall lights that stand on the floor.

entries.clue: Lowly employee finally quitting after endless stress (9)

indicatorNotes.after: 'After' means following in order, so the G is written behind UNDERLIN

blocks.note: to underline is to stress; minus its last E

annotation.surface: A junior worker finally quits after relentless stress.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stress" looks like workplace pressure; it is a verb, to emphasise.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a slightly scornful tone: someone ranked beneath the boss.

entries.clue: Go too far in dealing with party (6)

blocks.note: 'over' as in 'a row over money', meaning dealing with

annotation.surface: Overstepping the mark when handling a political party.
annotation.walkthrough: "Party" suggests politics; a do is a social party.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taking something beyond the proper limit, as with overcooked food or overplayed acting.

entries.clue: A DJ neatly arranged to tour clubs contiguously (10)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: A DJ tidily planning a tour of back-to-back club nights.
annotation.walkthrough: "Clubs" reads as nightclubs for the DJ; it is the card suit.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjacently means next to each other, contiguously.

entries.clue: Music producer involved in Latina group’s retrospective (5)

indicatorNotes.involved in: the answer is inside the words

blocks.note: latiNA GROup read right to left

annotation.surface: A Latin girl group's record producer looks back.
annotation.walkthrough: "Music producer" suggests a person in a studio; it is an instrument that produces music.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the church keyboard instrument literally produces music, though the phrase suggests a person in a studio.
